pending_designs.name: core-c2r3a-atomic-composition-delete
pending_designs.status: OPENED 2026-08-10, NOT BUILT, NO OWNER. Filed as plan section 13.1 (main bdad9d0, PR #127). Pushback 6-A forbids UNWINDING a composition - removing a member, mutating the member set, demoting the flag - while dependents exist. It does NOT forbid destroying one WHOLE. Today remove_intergraph_edge/remove_intergraph_hyperedge refuse every removal when compositional=True, so a pipeline, milestone or plan can never be deleted, only hidden, and Local grows monotonically. ONE new operation: remove a compositional link AND the members no other composition anchors, in a single transaction; refuse if a member is anchored elsewhere or if the composition is itself a member of one not also being removed. remove_intergraph_hyperedge keeps refusing piecemeal removal so 6-A stays closed. The exclusivity check IS walk(UP) - C2R3's invalidation walk, one more consumer, not a second implementation. Also: remove_graph's compositional precheck refuses only when a compositional edge CROSSES the graph boundary, not on any incident one. Carries the ADR-0205 am-1.5 replacement text: 'A composition's membership can never change, and a composition cannot be unwound while anything depends on it. A composition CAN be destroyed, but only whole, and only when nothing else anchors any of its members.'

pending_designs.name: core-global-update-migration
pending_designs.status: OPENED 2026-08-10, NOT BUILT, NO OWNER. Filed as plan section 13.3 (main bdad9d0, PR #127). NOBODY OWNED WHAT HAPPENS TO A USER'S WORK WHEN GLOBAL UPDATES - a user teaches a pipeline over shipped capacities, the system replaces them, and today the pipeline breaks silently. Ruling: GLOBAL PRUNES (it is the shipped baseline and must not accumulate every version ever released, or every installation pays for elements it never used). The copy must precede the prune, so THE UPDATE PACKAGE CARRIES THE OUTGOING VERSIONS as well as the new ones; it is a transient input, discarded on completion, and Global retains nothing. Migration is VERSION-DRIVEN AND IDEMPOTENT, not event-driven: Global carries a baseline version, each Local records the version it last migrated to, and ONE mechanism has TWO callers - the update, and boot as the catch-up. Crash-safe and resumable. Per Local: stop if versions match; walk that Local UPWARD from each replaced element; COPY the replaced elements as NEW elements from the artifact recording original identity and version; REBUILD each affected Local ancestor as a NEW element bottom-up (members are frozen, an existing composition can never be repointed); ATOMICALLY DELETE the old chain top-down with the exclusivity check; record the version; notify the user. Copy downward, rebuild upward, delete the old chain whole. Local-on-Local structure untouched. Updates apply IN SEQUENCE, each package self-contained.

VERDICT: this one genuinely bites — it scans 226 modules and `test_package_is_scanned` already defended the scan-zero failure mode. Two defects found. (1) COVERAGE was narrow enough to miss the phrasings people actually write: of fourteen plausible ownership claims probed, FOURTEEN slipped through — `WSD ships the real catalog` (the pattern required the literal 'ships IN'), `owned by WSD` (only the hyphenated `WSD-owned` matched), `deferred to WSD` / `routed to WSD` / `blocked on WSD`, `WSD is responsible for`, `nilm owns`, `FOL provides`. SIX patterns added (ships/will-ship/shipped-by without the literal 'in'; `owned by <sub>`; deferred|routed|blocked|pending|waiting to/on/for <sub>; <sub> ... responsible; <sub> ... provides|owns; and the verb-then-subsystem mirror `will ship with <sub>` / `lands in <sub>`), each verified ZERO-hit across the 226 scanned modules, so broadening cost no cleanup tail. (2) The ALLOWLIST was INERT — raw pattern hits before allowlisting were already 0, so none of its five entries exempted anything, while `test_allowlist_entries_still_exist` asserted only that the exempted TEXT still existed, not that the entry was NEEDED. An allowlist could therefore rot to fully inert and stay green: the same defect class as the ADR guard, one level in. Entries removed; the test now asserts each entry is LOAD-BEARING (delete it, a violation must appear), plus a synthetic-input test proving the exemption mechanism itself works while the list is empty (exempts when the needle is near the hit; does NOT exempt for a different file or an absent needle). Standing lesson from both guards: A GREEN GUARD THAT CANNOT FAIL IS WORSE THAN NO GUARD — test the failure behaviour, not only the passing state.

recent.what: TWO defects in ConjunctionFinder.find, BOTH live on the CLI `execute` verb (mindsos_cli/commands/brain.py:687, the only shipped path reaching this finder). The class makes the same claim at two resolutions - phase 1 'a route exists', phase 2 'here is the route' - and the two disagreed. **D-B**: phase 2 re-tested producers with frozenset() (pipeline.py:430, :462), discarding phase 1's cycle stack, so a producer phase 1 had refused could still be selected during construction, including to feed itself; it then recursed to max_depth and raised. Composition was NON-MONOTONIC in the start set - adding an available input could make a compose FAIL. **D-E (new, was not in CORE_VERIFIED_FINDINGS)**: fired[cap_iri] is written AFTER a capacity's inputs are built, and the cycle stack tracks DataStates under resolution, not capacities under construction - so mid-fire() a capacity is in neither guard and can be selected to produce one of its own transitive inputs. It then either recursed to max_depth, OR completed and was appended to steps TWICE: find() returned a Pipeline naming one capacity as two distinct steps, with no error, and execute_pipeline ran it twice while the one-slot-per-DataState-IRI blackboard (D-C) silently overwrote the first result. **D-B raised; D-E lied.** D-E also falsified the class docstring's own claim that shared upstream producers fire once. **The fix**: phase-2 admission moves into one predicate with three clauses in order - refuse a capacity that is in_flight; admit one that has already fired (reusing its step index); otherwise fall through to phase 1's predicate WITH THE LIVE CYCLE STACK. fire() carries the stack and maintains an in_flight set. No signature, declaration or result-shape change; no capacity gains a field. **Evidence, not argument** (the owner's instruction): confirmation_docs/finder_variants_model.py reproduces both phases exactly and swaps only the admission rule - over 20,000 generated capacity graphs, the shipped rule and a stack-only fix both leave 369 max_depth blowups and 20 duplicate-step pipelines; with the in_flight guard, 0 and 0. The three shipped conformance shapes (all_required AND, diamond convergence, fold fan-in) are byte-identical across all variants. Separately measured: the `fired` short-circuit in eligible() is a COST optimisation, not a correctness clause - identical results with and without it in all 20,000 graphs - and is documented as such rather than defended as one. 4 new tests assert BEHAVIOUR not implementation and carry a header saying so.

No structural blobs. AND is within a composition, OR is several compositions sharing an anchor (no new edge type). Lazy descent: the MM loads the highest level and drops one only for the nodes it needs. Structure is stable, learning moves confidence. A Skill spans ALL levels - install/uninstall is the whole vertical; uninstall keeps the user's data and leaves taught structure DORMANT.
